description: Gilead Sciences is a biopharmaceutical company that researches, develops, and commercializes medicines. Gilead’s Veklury (remdesivir) was one of the first antiviral treatments authorized for COVID-19. Gilead also pioneered groundbreaking treatments for HIV that helped transform the fatal virus into a manageable chronic condition. The company continues to expand into oncology and other chronic conditions through acquisitions, such as CymaBay, which developed a treatment for a rare liver disease.

title: Gilead Sciences

rankings.title: Change the World
rankings.itemDescription: Gilead is a longtime leader in HIV therapeutics and prevention, including antiretroviral treatment and pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) medicines, which are drugs taken to lower the risk of contracting HIV. Gilead has worked with the government of South Africa and the Global Fund to accelerate access to lenacapavir, a long-acting prevention medication that the FDA approved in 2022 to treat drug-resistant HIV. Approximately 7.8 million people in South Africa live with HIV, with an estimated 170,000 new infections each year.

rankings.title: Change the World
rankings.itemDescription: Gilead’s drugs have helped change HIV infection from a death sentence to a manageable condition. In 2012, it launched the first pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) preventive drug for HIV. In June, it won FDA approval for Yeztugo, a PrEP drug requiring only two doses a year—giving it far greater potential efficacy in preventing new infections.

rankings.title: Change the World
rankings.itemDescription: Although the southern United States represent only 33% of the U.S. population, they account for 51% of new HIV diagnoses and 47% of HIV-related deaths in the country. Gilead, which makes a variety of HIV drugs, has launched the Compass Initiative to tackle the factors fueling that disparity. In partnership with more than 390 community organizations across 16 states, Compass’s events and training programs focus on topics including stigma reduction and trauma-informed medical care, with the aim of helping those community groups do more to help combat the spread of HIV. To date, Compass has provided 300,000 people with services, trained 26,000 individuals in leadership development, and provided more than $106 million in grant funding to support outreach to those impacted by HIV.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: The biopharmaceutical company researches and develops antiviral drugs used in the treatment of life-threatening diseases, including HIV and hepatitis. Last October, its intravenous drug remdesivir became the first treatment for COVID-19 approved for emergency use by the FDA.
